subject: zoology
question_text: Name the three meninges. In which group of animals do you find all of them?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.56, VSAQ 123). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three meninges
steps.margin_note: Three names with outer, middle and inner marked. That is the first mark.
lines: Meninges are the membranes that cover the brain
The three meninges, from outside inwards, are:
steps.why: The three names are always asked in order from outside inwards, so writing the order into the answer protects the mark even if one name is misspelt.
common_mistakes: Naming only duramater and piamater. The arachnoid is the middle one and completes the three.
Reversing the order. Duramater is the outermost and piamater the innermost.
steps.memory_tip: Hard outside, cobweb in the middle, soft inside: dura, arachnoid, pia.

steps.label: The group
steps.margin_note: One word answers the second half. The amphibian contrast is a short bonus line.

lines.text: All three meninges are found in mammals

lines: All three meninges are found in mammals.
In amphibians there are only two, the
steps.why: The second half of the question is a single word answer, and the amphibian line is the contrast that shows the answer was not a guess.
common_mistakes: Answering vertebrates. Not all vertebrates have three; the answer is mammals.
Writing that amphibians have three. Amphibians have two.
steps.memory_tip: Three membranes for the group with the biggest brain: mammals.

insider_note: Two halves, one mark each — the group is a single word, so an answer with three perfect names and no group still loses half the paper's credit.
